target_customer: Owners of small and mid-sized businesses (company says $5M to $100M in sales) who want to sell, plus institutional buyers
problem: Small businesses are too small for traditional investment banks and are left to brokers or going it alone. OffDeal uses AI to do analyst-style buyer matching and outreach so a small advisor team can run auction-style sales cheaply.
business_model: Success fee on the transaction (TechCrunch reported 5% to 10% of transaction value in Sept 2024); no upfront fee per company site
product_category: AI-enabled M&A advisory (sell-side investment bank for small businesses)

founders.name: Ori Eldarov
founders.background_notes: YC page: prior startup and finance experience; tried and failed to acquire a business in 2019, which led to the problem. TechCrunch calls him a former investment banker.

founders.name: Alston Lin
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; some employers were internships or software engineer roles.

technical_complexity.rationale: Buyer matching, data on millions of small businesses and automated outreach with LLMs are standard engineering with some hard parts; the harder part is running a licensed advisory business, not the software.

defensibility.rationale: Buyer database and advisor relationships compound, and brokerage work needs people and trust, but AI matching alone is copyable. TechCrunch (Sept 2024) cited nine institutional buyers under contract and 250 on a waitlist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the wedge by the end of the sources checked (late 2026 search found no acquisition news).

market_need_then: Traditional investment banks ignore small deals and brokers are fragmented. The company claims a database of 2 million US small businesses that may sell (TechCrunch, Sept 2024).

branding.domain_note: Uses offdeal.io rather than .com; acquisition date not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Modern, direct and warm to owners; taglines 'Time kills deals. We save both.' and 'We only win if you win.'

branding.brand_signature: Positioning line 'The investment bank for small businesses' and the 'AI-native investment bank' framing.
branding.community_and_virality: A Sourcery newsletter piece described the Series A announcement as going viral on social media; the company lists coverage from WSJ, CNBC, FT, Forbes and TechCrunch on its site.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press coverage and a clear category claim, but no mascot or community; name is plain and descriptive of dealmaking.

pivots.from: AI broker to help individual buyers find and acquire small businesses (YC launch post framing)
pivots.to: AI-native investment bank for sellers of small businesses
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; the change is inferred from the YC launch title versus later positioning.

outcome_analysis: OffDeal raised a $4.7M seed in September 2024 and a $12M Series A in July 2025 led by Radical Ventures, within about ten months, which signals fast traction in AI-enabled small business M&A. It remains active and no exit or Series B was found. Success rests on a founder who lived the problem, an engineering partner from large tech and a model where AI supplements human advisors.
notes: Seed amount confirmed by TechCrunch (one outlet; another profile rounds to $5M). Series A confirmed by company post and Finextra. A search summary claimed a roughly $100M post-money valuation from a single aggregator; the company post says valuation not disclosed, so not recorded. A StartupHub listing showing $1M raised and 2022 founding conflicts with all other sources. Competitor search returned only undated pages; TechCrunch (Sept 2024) named no direct competitors, only traditional banks and small business brokers, so the list is empty. Seed date from TechCrunch publication date.
